t001.name: Bukhansan Dulle-gil Trail: Sonamusup-gil, Sullye-gil & Huingureum-gil
t001.sub: Forest trail on the east side of Bukhansan, Ui-dong → Jeongneung
t001.start: Ui-dong Mannam Plaza (near the start of Sonamusup-gil)
t001.how: About 5 min walk from Bukhansan Ui Station (Ui LRT Line)
t001.turn: One-way — from the end point (Bukhansan Ecological Forest), return by city bus toward Jeongneung or via the Ui LRT Line (toward Solsaem Station)
points: Sullye-gil around the National 4·19 Democracy Cemetery
Entrance to the Tomb of Patriot Yi Jun (Sullye-gil → Huingureum-gil)
t001.notes: Section distances (3.1 + 2.3 + 4.1 km) follow the usual national park Dulle-gil listings and could not be re-verified directly on the official page. Largely overlaps with Seoul Dulle-gil Course 20 (Hwagyesa entrance – Bukhansan Ui Station).
events: Gangbuk-gu 'Good Walking Roads' online stamp tour (includes the 4.3 km Bukhansan Dulle-gil stretch from Ui-dong Mannam Plaza to the Tomb of Patriot Yi Jun entrance; souvenir on completion)
Overlaps with Seoul Dulle-gil Course 20 (Bukhansan Gangbuk Course, 7.1 km) — completion certificate and badge for collecting all 28 Seoul Dulle-gil stamps

t002.name: Bukhansan Uiryeong-gil Trail
t002.sub: Pass between Ui-dong and Gyohyeon-ri, closed for 50 years
t002.how: From Suyu Station (Line 4) or Bukhansan Ui Station (Ui LRT Line), go by bus or on foot to the Ui-dong terminus, then walk
t002.turn: One-way — from the Gyohyeon-ri side, return by bus (No. 704 or 34 to Gupabal Station) or walk back
t002.toiletNote: 3 locations, including the Ui entrance and the visitor centers (per blog reports). No drinking fountains or shops along the trail
t002.notes: From April 2026, open on weekdays (Mon–Fri) without reservation; weekends and public holidays require a national park reservation (1,000 people/day, 500 each at Ui and Gyohyeon). Residents of Gangbuk, Dobong and Yangju may pass freely after a one-time on-site registration. Entry 09:00–14:00; descend by 16:00. Bring ID.

t003.name: Seoul City Wall Trail (Hanyangdoseong), Full Circuit
t003.sub: Loop over the four inner mountains: Baegak, Naksan, Namsan, Inwangsan
t003.notes: Sections: Baegak 4.7 km (hard), Naksan 2.1 km (easy), Namsan 4.2 km (moderate), Inwang 4.0 km (hard), plus the downtown sections around Heunginjimun and Sungnyemun. Baegak and Inwang are hard, with many stairs.
events: Seoul City Wall completion certification: photos at the 4 inner-mountain spots → apply on the website → certificate and seasonal badge at the Seoul City Wall Museum / Hyehwa-dong Exhibition & Information Center (metal badge for completing all 4 seasons; once per quarter)
District 'Seoul City Wall Stamp Tour' (4 spots: Heunginjimun, Sungnyemun, Donuimun site, Sukjeongmun → white badge; separate from the mayor's certificate)

t004.name: Seoul City Wall Trail: Baegak Section
t004.how: From Gyeongbokgung Station (Line 3), take a city bus (7022, 7212, etc.) to Jahamun Pass / Yun Dong-ju Literary Museum
t004.turn: One-way — from Hyehwamun, 5 min walk to Hansung University Station (Line 4)
t004.notes: Open year-round; recommended visiting hours vary by season (check the website). Hard — many stairs.
events: Seoul City Wall completion certification (includes the Baegak Cheongundae · Baegakmaru photo spot)

t005.name: Seoul City Wall Trail: Inwangsan Section
t005.how: About 5 min walk from Exit 4, Seodaemun Station (Line 5)
t005.turn: One-way — from Changuimun (Jahamun Pass), return to Gyeongbokgung Station by city bus
points: Near the Yun Dong-ju Literary Museum
t005.notes: Hard (rocky ridges, stairs). Names of intermediate waypoints follow general guides.
events: Seoul City Wall completion certification (Inwangsan summit photo spot)

t006.name: Namsan Northern Circular Road
t006.start: Plaza in front of the National Theater of Korea
t006.how: From Exit 6, Dongguk University Station (Line 3), take the Namsan shuttle bus or walk about 15 min
t006.end: Near Namsan Library (toward the Namsan Cable Car)
t006.turn: One-way — from Namsan Library, take a city bus or walk toward Sungnyemun or Myeong-dong
t006.notes: Northern Circular Road about 3 km (per Seoul city article; measured 3.4 km from the National Theater toward the cable car). Always open, free. Inquiries: Jungbu Park & Greenery Office 02-3783-5900.

t007.name: Ansan Jarak-gil Trail
t007.sub: Korea's first barrier-free loop forest trail
t007.how: About 5 min walk from Exits 4 & 5, Dongnimmun Station (Line 3) (also accessible from Muakjae Station, Hongje Station and Seodaemun-gu Office)
t007.toiletNote: No toilets on the course — use nearby toilets beforehand, e.g. at Dongnimmun Station or Seodaemun-gu Office (per Teltrip article)
t007.notes: Entire course is decking with gentle slopes, suitable for wheelchairs and strollers. No drinking fountains or shops. Free and always open. There is no official 'starting point' — Independence Park is designated for convenience.

t008.name: Seoul Dulle-gil Trail 2.0, Full Circuit
t008.sub: 21-course loop around the outskirts of Seoul
t008.hours: Average about 8 km per course — several days for the full circuit
t008.start: Dobongsan Station Exit 2 · Seoul Changpowon (start of Course 1, Suraksan Course)
t008.how: Exit 2, Dobongsan Station (Lines 1 & 7), right next to the Seoul Changpowon Information Center
t008.turn: Loop — walked in 21 courses, each ending at a subway station (43 stations in all)
points: Seoul Changpowon Information Center (stamp books available)
Course 1 end, Danggogae Park junction (Buramsan Station)
Gwangnaru Station (stamp books at the Achasan Management Office)
t008.notes: The 2.0 reorganization expanded it from 8 to 21 courses; Course 1 (Suraksan Course) is 6.3 km, 2 h 50 min. Stamp books at the City Hall Open Civil Service Center, Changpowon, Maeheon Citizens' Forest, Achasan and Gwanaksan information centers. Inquiries 02-779-7902~4. The list of intermediate stations is based on the hubs of the old 8 courses.
events: Collect all 28 stamps across the 21 Seoul Dulle-gil courses → completion certificate + commemorative badge

t009.name: Achasan Goguryeo History Trail
t009.how: Exit 1, Gwangnaru Station (Line 5) → about 10 min walk to the Achasan entrance
t009.end: Han River Bicycle Park (toward the south end of Gwangjingyo Bridge)
t009.turn: One-way, but the end is near Gwangnaru Station — walk back to the station
points: Achasan Ecological Park · Goguryeo History & Culture Center
t009.notes: Corrected the draft's 'starts at Achasan Ecological Park' — per the Academy of Korean Studies, the start is Gwangnaru Station and the Ecological Park is an intermediate waypoint. Consists of 2 courses.

t010.name: Gyeongui Line Forest Park
t010.sub: Urban linear park on a disused railway
t010.start: Saechanggogae (Hyochang-dong, east end of the Gyeongui Line Forest Park)
t010.how: About 5 min walk from Hyochang Park Station (Line 6 · Gyeongui–Jungang Line)
t010.end: End of the Yeonnam-dong section (toward Gajwa Station)
t010.turn: One-way — from the end, return via Gajwa Station (Gyeongui–Jungang Line) or Hongik Univ. Station
points: Gyeongui Line Book Street (Hongik Univ. Station)
t010.notes: Extended the draft's 'Gongdeok → Gajwa' to the official full length (Yeonnam-dong – Hyochang-dong, 6.3 km; 5.12 km of park) — Gongdeok Station is an intermediate waypoint. Interrupted into 6 sections by roads and stations.

t011.name: Haneul Park · Noeul Park Metasequoia Road
t011.sub: 2.3 km green tunnel and silver grass at World Cup Park
t011.hours: 1 h 30 min – 2 hours (including round trip from the station)
t011.how: 15 min walk from Exit 1, World Cup Stadium Station (Line 6) (18 min from Exit 8, Mapo-gu Office Station)
t011.end: End of the Metasequoia Road toward Noeul Park
t011.turn: Walk back from the end of the Metasequoia Road, or climb the Z-shaped stairs to the Haneul Park silver grass field and return to the station
points: Haneul Park Metasequoia Road (original east side)
Z-shaped stairs (to the upper level of Haneul Park)
Metasequoia Road toward Noeul Park (opened May 2026)
t011.notes: A 1 km forest road toward Noeul Park opened on 2026-05-22, for a total of 2.3 km. Parking at Peace Park and Nanjicheon Park (paid). Crowded during the silver grass festival — public transport recommended.
events: 25th Seoul Silver Grass Festival (Haneul Park, 10:00–21:00) — ongoing

t012.name: Suwon Hwaseong Fortress Wall Trail
t012.sub: A full lap of the World Heritage fortress wall
t012.how: From Suwon Station, take a city bus to Janganmun (or walk about 15 min from Suwon Station to the wall and enter from the Paldalsan side)
t012.notes: The wall is 5.74 km around. Walking the wall is free and always open (per Teltrip article); Hwaseong Haenggung Palace is paid (adults ₩2,000). Public parking nearby is paid.
events: 63rd Suwon Hwaseong Cultural Festival (around Haenggung Square and Hwaseong Haenggung Palace) — ended

t013.name: Namhansanseong Fortress Wall Circuit (Course 5, Sanseong-ui Gil)
t013.sub: A full lap of the World Heritage mountain fortress
t013.how: From Sanseong Station (Line 8), take a city bus bound for Namhansanseong (No. 9, etc.) → get off at Sanseong Rotary and walk to the South Gate
t013.notes: The official start of Course 5 is the Namhansanseong World Heritage Center (Sanseong Rotary) — as it is a loop, starting at the South Gate is the same. Free entry. Inquiries 031-8008-5155. Check bus routes before travelling.

t014.name: Yangpyeong Dumulmeori Mullae-gil Trail
t014.sub: Riverside path at the confluence of the South and North Han Rivers
t014.how: About 10 min walk from Yangsu Station (Gyeongui–Jungang Line)
t014.turn: Loop (based on the 10 km walking festival course; a 6 km shortcut is available)
t014.notes: Distance based on the Yangpyeong-gun walking festival course — official distance of the permanent course not confirmed. The start is not Yangsu Station but the nearby Yangseo Culture & Sports Park.
events: Dumulmeori Mullae-gil Walking Festival every autumn (check dates; held on 15 Oct 2022)

t015.name: Pyeonghwa Nuri-gil Trail, Gimpo Course 3: Han River Fence Road
t015.sub: Han River estuary and migratory birds beyond the military fence
t015.how: From a Gimpo Goldline station, take a city bus toward Haseong-myeon (check routes)
t015.turn: One-way — from Jeollyu-ri Port, return to central Gimpo by city bus
t015.notes: Course 3 follows Gimpo Course 1 (Yeomhagang Fence Road) and Course 2 (Jogang Fence Road) (recommended for December by Gyeonggi-do). The 17 km distance is from the draft and was not re-verified on the official page this time. Fence sections may be closed for military operations.

t016.name: Gwanggyo Lake Park Dulle-gil Trail
t016.sub: Loops around Woncheon and Sindae Lakes
t016.how: About 20 min walk from Gwanggyo Jungang Station (Shinbundang Line) to Woncheon Lake (20 min from Sanghyeon Station to Sindae Lake)
points: Freiburg Observatory (33 m, café on 1st floor)
Toilet on the 1st floor of Freiburg Observatory
t016.toiletNote: 1st floor of Freiburg Observatory (per Teltrip article). Other locations unconfirmed
t016.notes: Free. 3 car parks (first 3 hours ₩1,000, max ₩5,000 per day).

t017.name: Paju Majang Lake Suspension Bridge Dulle-gil Trail
t017.sub: 220 m suspension bridge and waterside decks
t017.start: Majang Lake car park (Car Parks 1–3, near the suspension bridge)
t017.how: Public transport is inconvenient — driving recommended (bus routes not confirmed)
points: Suspension bridge (220 m, 18 m glass section)
Shops and cafés near the observatory
t017.notes: Perimeter deck 3.6 km (corrected from the draft's 3.3 km, per Teltrip article). 7 car parks, max ₩2,000 per day. Suspension bridge opening hours and closing days not confirmed.

t018.name: Pocheon Hantangang River Columnar Joint Trail: Bidulginang Loop
t018.sub: Bidulginang Waterfall and the Hantangang River gorge
t018.how: Driving recommended (Bidulginang Waterfall car park). Public transport information not confirmed
t018.notes: All 5 Pocheon Columnar Joint Trail courses (Guraigil 4 km, Gamasogil 5 km, Byeorutgil 6 km, Meongurigil 5 km, Bidulginang Loop 6 km) start at Bidulginang Waterfall. Inquiries 031-538-2312.

t019.name: Daebu Haesol-gil Trail, Course 1
t019.sub: Pine forest, Gaemi-heori Arch Bridge, sunset at Gubongdo
t019.how: From Ansan Station (Line 4), bus No. 123 for about 40 min, get off at Bangameori Wharf
t019.turn: One-way — return by bus from Gubongdo Public Car Park
t019.notes: Gaemi-heori Arch Bridge is accessible only at low tide — check the tide table. 3 free car parks.

t020.name: Ganghwa Nadeul-gil Trail, Course 1: Simdo History & Culture Trail
t020.sub: Goryeo Palace Site, Anglican Church, Yeonmijeong Pavilion
t020.how: From Sinchon Station (Line 2) or elsewhere, take an express/intercity bus to Ganghwa Bus Terminal
t020.turn: One-way — from Gapgot Dondae, return to the terminal by city bus
t020.notes: There is a place to get a completion stamp (exact location not stated — check with Nadeul-gil, 032-934-1906).

t021.name: Ganghwa Nadeul-gil Trail, Course 2: Hogukdondae-gil
t021.sub: Forts and garrisons along the Yeomha Channel
t021.how: From Ganghwa Bus Terminal, about 10 min by city bus or taxi
t021.turn: One-way — from Chojijin (Onsu Intersection), return to Ganghwa Terminal by bus
t021.notes: There is a place to get a completion stamp (location not stated). Inquiries 032-934-1906.

t022.name: Muuido Hanagae Seaside Trail
t022.sub: Sea deck path below the cliffs of Horyonggoksan
t022.how: From Incheon Airport Terminal 1, bus Muui 1 for about 30 min, get off at Hanagae Beach
t022.end: End of the seaside trail (Horyonggoksan cliffs)
t022.turn: Out-and-back — return from the end of the deck (about 800 m)
t022.toiletNote: 4 locations: Hanagae Beach, Gwangmyeong Port, Somuuido entrance, Mongyeo Beach (Teltrip). None on the trail itself
t022.notes: Deck about 800 m; free and open year-round; closed in bad weather — check the tide table. Parking ₩4,000 per day. The full 'Muuido Dulle-gil' course could not be confirmed in official sources, so this entry focuses on the seaside trail — can be combined with a Horyonggoksan hike or Somuuido.

t023.name: Daegwallyeong Seonjaryeong Windmill Trail
t023.sub: Baekdudaegan grasslands on Gangneung Baugil Section 1
t023.start: Daegwallyeong Village Rest Area (former Daegwallyeong Rest Area)
t023.how: About 10 min by taxi from Hoenggye Intercity Bus Terminal
t023.notes: Starts at about 850 m elevation, so slopes are gentle, but the weather changes quickly — bring extra layers. Famous for winter snow scenery. Closure during forest-fire prevention periods not officially confirmed — check with Baugil or the National Forest Management Office before visiting.

t024.name: Olympic Ari Baugil Trail, Course 7
t024.sub: Royal-decree pine road (Bohyeonsa → Tomb of King Myeongju)
t024.how: From central Gangneung, take the city bus to Bohyeonsa and get off at the terminus (check routes)
t024.turn: One-way — from the Tomb of King Myeongju, return to Gangneung by city bus
points: Eomyeongjeong (stump of the Geumgang pine used to restore Gwanghwamun)
t024.notes: The whole Ari Baugil has 9 courses, 131.7 km (Jeongseon 5-Day Market – Gyeongpo Beach). Moderate difficulty. Inquiries: Gangneung Baugil 033-645-0990.

t025.name: Daegwallyeong Old Road
t025.start: Banjeong (below the former Daegwallyeong Rest Area)
t025.how: Public transport information not confirmed — drive and use the former Daegwallyeong Rest Area car park
t025.turn: One-way — from the museum, return by Gangneung city bus or taxi
t025.notes: Mostly a gentle downhill dirt path. No admission or parking fees. Overlaps with Gangneung Baugil Section 2.

t026.name: Jeongdong-Simgok Badabuchae-gil Trail
t026.sub: Deck path on a coastal terrace designated a Natural Monument
t026.how: From Jeongdongjin Station (Yeongdong Line), by taxi or on foot (toward Sun Cruise)
t026.turn: One-way — from Simgok Port, return to Jeongdongjin by taxi or bus, or walk back
t026.toiletNote: Toilets and parking at the ticket office areas (Korea Tourism Organization)
t026.notes: Paid: adults ₩5,000, youth ₩4,000, children ₩3,000. Summer (Apr–Oct) 09:00–17:30 (tickets until 16:30); winter 09:00–16:30 (tickets until 15:30). Open year-round but closed during high-wave advisories/warnings; may change due to military operations. Trail 2.86 km (3.01 km between ticket offices). Jeongdong 033-641-9444 / Simgok 033-641-9445.

t027.name: Odaesan Seonjae-gil Trail
t027.how: From Jinbu Intercity Bus Terminal, take the bus to Woljeongsa/Sangwonsa
t027.turn: One-way — from Sangwonsa, return to Woljeongsa/Jinbu by bus (can also be walked downhill in reverse, Sangwonsa → Woljeongsa)
t027.notes: Woljeongsa – Dongpigol 5.4 km (2 h 10 min), Dongpigol – Sangwonsa 3.6 km (1 h 20 min). Flooding and closures during summer downpours — Odaesan Office 033-332-6417. Parking ₩3,000.

t028.name: Inje Wondae-ri Birch Forest
t028.hours: 3–4 hours (forest road round trip + forest walk)
t028.how: About 15 min by taxi from Inje Intercity Bus Terminal (public transport routes not confirmed)
t028.turn: Loop — up via the Wonjeong Forest Road, down via the Wondae Forest Road
points: Wonjeong Forest Road (about 80 min on foot)
t028.toiletNote: Toilets available (separate men's/women's, Korea Tourism Organization) — exact location presumed to be near the information center
t028.notes: Closed Mon & Tue (open if a public holiday). Entry May–Oct 09:00–15:00, Nov–Feb 09:00–14:00. Closed during the spring forest-fire prevention period — reopened 1 May in 2026. For autumn closures, check with the Inje National Forest Management Office (033-463-0044). The 7 km total is an estimate based on forest-road walking times (official distance unconfirmed).

t029.name: Seoraksan: Sogongwon → Biseondae
t029.sub: Past Sinheungsa and Waseondae to the valley's rock beds
t029.how: From central Sokcho, city bus No. 7 or 7-1 to the Seoraksan terminus
t029.turn: Out-and-back — return from Biseondae (6 km round trip)
t029.toiletNote: Toilet at Sogongwon (marked 'toilet available' by the Korea Tourism Organization). Biseondae side unconfirmed
t029.notes: Beyond Biseondae (toward Madeungnyeong, Huiungak, Yeongsiam) is closed during the forest-fire prevention periods: spring 2 Mar–15 May, autumn 1 Nov–15 Dec. Sogongwon – Biseondae is low-lying and stays open. Cultural heritage area admission fee abolished from 2023-05-04 (parking charged separately).
events: Seorak International Trekking Festival — ended

t030.name: Seoraksan Jujeongol Valley
t030.how: Bus to Osaek from Yangyang, Sokcho or Dong Seoul; get off at Osaek
t030.turn: Out-and-back — return from Yongso Falls (6.4 km round trip), or exit at Yongso Falls Visitor Center onto National Route 44
t030.toiletNote: Toilets available (Korea Tourism Organization; location not stated)
t030.notes: Hours: summer (Mar–Oct) 03:00–17:30, winter 04:00–17:30. Being low-lying, not subject to the autumn high-altitude closure (15 Nov–15 Dec) (2025 article). Some connecting sections (e.g. Osaek Mineral Spring – Manggyeongdae) have separate closures — Osaek Branch Office 033-672-2883.
events: Seorak International Trekking Festival — ended

t031.name: Chuncheon Kim Yu-jeong Sille Story Trail
t031.sub: Bomnae-gil Course 1, the Sille Village of Kim Yu-jeong's stories
t031.how: About 5 min walk from Gimyujeong Station (Gyeongchun Line)
t031.notes: Includes some mountain paths on the slopes of Geumbyeongsan. Details of the '16 spots' along the way could not be confirmed in official sources.

t032.name: Wonju Sogeumsan Grand Valley
t032.sub: Suspension bridge, Sogeum cliff walkway, Ulleong Bridge
t032.how: From Wonju Station or Wonju Terminal, take a city bus toward Ganhyeon (check routes)
t032.turn: One-way mountain course — crossing Ulleong Bridge and descending brings you back near the start
t032.notes: Trekking course ₩10,000 (includes suspension bridge, cliff walkway and Ulleong Bridge); cable car course ₩18,000 (per blogs; official confirmation needed). May–Oct 09:00–18:00, Nov–Apr 09:00–17:00; closed Mondays.
events: Wonju International Walking Festival every October (check dates; 31st edition 25–26 Oct 2025 along the Wonjucheon riverside)

t033.name: Chiaksan: Guryongsa → Seryeom Falls
t033.sub: Hwangjangmok pine forest path, Guryongso valley
t033.how: From central Wonju, city bus No. 41 to the Guryongsa terminus
points: Guryongso (barrier-free section of the Hwangjangmok forest path)
t033.toiletNote: Toilets available (Korea Tourism Organization; location not stated)
t033.notes: Distance figures vary — the Korea Tourism Organization gives '3 km round trip, 1 h 30 min'. Entry: summer 04:00–14:00, winter 05:00–13:00. The valley next to Seryeom Falls is open temporarily in summer. Inquiries 033-740-9900.
events: Wonju International Walking Festival every October (check dates)

t034.name: Cheorwon Hantangang River Columnar Joint Trail (Cliff Walkway)
t034.sub: 3.6 km walkway suspended from the cliffs
t034.how: Taxi from Dongsong or Sincheorwon terminals. Shuttle bus between the two entrances on weekends
t034.turn: One-way — return to the start by the weekend shuttle bus (on weekdays, walk back or take a taxi)
t034.notes: Admission adults ₩10,000 (₩5,000 refunded as Cheorwon gift vouchers), children ₩4,000. Mar–Nov 09:00–16:00, Dec–Feb 09:00–15:00. Closed every Tuesday, 1 Jan, and on Seollal and Chuseok days; suspended during heavy-rain advisories. Sundam 0507-1431-2225 / Deureuni 0507-1374-9825.

t035.name: Gangneung Gyeongpo Lake Dulle-gil Trail
t035.how: From Gangneung Station or the intercity bus terminal, take a city bus toward Gyeongpo (No. 202 series)
points: Heo Gyun · Heo Nanseolheon Memorial Park
Chamsori Museum (Gyeongpo Lake view from 3rd floor)
t035.notes: The lake circumference of about 4.3 km is the commonly cited distance; official figure unconfirmed. Gasiyeon Wetland entry and parking are free.
events: Gangneung Gyeongpo Cherry Blossom Festival every April (check dates)

t036.name: Taebaek Manhangjae → Hambaeksan
t036.sub: From a 1,330 m pass reachable by car to the 1,573 m summit
t036.how: Taxi from Gohan or Taebaek (public transport routes not confirmed)
t036.turn: Out-and-back — return from the summit to Manhangjae (or continue along the ridge toward Junghambaek and Dumundongjae)
points: Steep section just below the summit
t036.notes: 243 m elevation gain, with a steep pitch just below the summit. The distance of about 3 km is an estimate from hiking reports — official figure unconfirmed. Ice and rime frost in winter.
events: Wildflower festival around Manhangjae every summer (check dates)

t037.name: Songnisan Sejo-gil Trail
t037.sub: Past Beopjusa to the reservoir and Sesimjeong
t037.how: Bus to Songnisan from Boeun Terminal or Cheongju; about 15 min walk from Songnisan Terminal
t037.turn: Out-and-back — return from Sesimjeong (can be extended toward Munjangdae: Sesimjeong – Munjangdae about 6.6 km round trip)
t037.notes: Distance figures vary: 2.35 km at opening (ticket office – Sesimjeong); Teltrip says 'about 4 km'. Beopjusa cultural heritage admission fee abolished 2023-05-04 — free.

t038.name: Cheongju Cheongnamdae Presidential Trail
t038.sub: Promenade at the former presidential villa along Daecheongho Lake
t038.how: Cheongju city bus to Munui Cultural Heritage Complex, then onward (infrequent service — driving recommended)
t038.turn: Loop — choose from the 6 Presidential Trails and return to the main building
points: Ogakjeong Pavilion (350 m from the main building)
t038.notes: Admission adults ₩6,000, youth ₩4,000, children & seniors ₩3,000. Feb–Nov 09:00–18:00 (last entry 16:30), Dec–Jan 09:00–17:00 (last entry 15:30). Closed Mondays, 1 Jan, and on Seollal and Chuseok days. Advance reservation not required. 13.5 km is the total length of the promenades (per blogs) — individual Presidential Trail distances not officially confirmed.

t039.name: Chungju Binae-gil Trail, Section 1
t039.sub: Silver-grass riverside of Binaeseom Island on the South Han River
t039.how: From central Chungju, take a city bus toward Angseong (check routes); parking available
t039.notes: Section 2 (11 km, 4 h 30 min) is a loop via Neungam Hot Spring Land, Saebajisan Observatory and Binaeseom. Free, open year-round. Inquiries 043-842-0531.

t040.name: Danyanggang Cliff Walkway · Mancheonha Skywalk
t040.sub: Cliffside walkway and observatory over the South Han River
t040.start: Danyanggang Cliff Walkway entrance (near Mancheonha Skywalk Car Park 2)
t040.how: Taxi or on foot from Danyang Station or Danyang Terminal (check routes)
t040.turn: Out-and-back — return from the end of the walkway (about 1 hour round trip); combine with Mancheonha Skywalk
t040.notes: Walkway free; night lighting from sunset to 23:00. Skywalk adults ₩4,000, youth ₩3,000; summer (Apr–Oct) 09:00–18:00, winter 09:00–17:00; attractions closed every Tuesday; suspended in strong winds or heavy rain.

t041.name: Cheongpungho Jadeurak-gil Trail, Course 6: Goegok Fortress Wall Road
t041.sub: Mountain paths via Oksun Bridge, Dabul-ri and Jigok-ri
t041.how: Driving recommended (check Jecheon city bus routes)
t041.turn: Loop (Kyunghyang Shinmun, 2013) — some guides also mention a boat link from Jigok-ri to Oksun Bridge (about 4 km, 20 min)
points: Dabul-ri ('the first village under the sky')
t041.toiletNote: Toilet at the Oksunbong car park (Korea Tourism Organization's Oksunbong guide). On the course itself unconfirmed
t041.notes: Rated 'hard' among the 7 Jadeurak-gil courses (58 km). Start/end points differ between sources — check with the Jecheon Tourist Information Center (043-641-4731) before visiting.

t042.name: Taean Coastal Trail, Course 1: Bara-gil
t042.how: From Taean Public Bus Terminal, take the county bus to Hagampo
t042.turn: One-way — from Sinduri, return to Taean by county bus
t042.toiletNote: Car park and toilets available (Korea Tourism Organization; location not stated)
t042.notes: Taean Coastal Trail: 7 courses, 97 km (Taeanhaean National Park). Inquiries 041-670-2543.

t043.name: Taean Coastal Trail, Course 5: Noeul-gil
t043.sub: Baeksajang Port → Kkotji's Halmi & Harabi Rocks
t043.how: From Taean Terminal, take the bus to Anmyeondo; get off at Baeksajang
t043.turn: One-way — return by bus from Kkotji
t043.notes: Names of intermediate waypoints follow general guides (official page not confirmed). Aim to reach Kkotji around sunset.

t044.name: Taean Coastal Trail, Course 4: Solmorae-gil
t044.how: From Taean Terminal, take a county bus toward Mongsanpo
t044.turn: One-way — from Deureuni Port, cross the Daeharang Kkotgerang footbridge to Baeksajang Port to connect with Noeul-gil (Course 5)
t044.notes: Names of intermediate waypoints follow general guides (official page not confirmed).

t045.name: Gongju Gongsanseong Fortress Wall Trail
t045.sub: Royal fortress of Ungjin-era Baekje, Geumgang River views
t045.how: From Gongju Bus Terminal, cross Geumgang Bridge and walk about 25 min, or take a city bus
t045.notes: Admission adults ₩3,000, youth ₩2,000, children ₩1,000. Mar–Oct entry until 18:00; Nov–Feb closes 17:00 (tickets until 16:30). Free parking at Geumseoru and Gongbukru.
events: 72nd Baekje Cultural Festival (around Geumgang Singwan Park and Gongsanseong in Gongju; night show at Gongsanseong) — ended

t046.name: Buyeo Busosanseong Fortress
t046.sub: Nakhwaam Rock, Goransa Temple, Hwangpo sailboats on the Baengmagang River
t046.how: About 15 min walk from Buyeo Intercity Bus Terminal
t046.turn: Round trip (ticket office – Nakhwaam 1.1 km one-way) — or return to Gudeure Ferry by Hwangpo sailboat from Goransa pier
t046.notes: Admission: adults ₩2,000, youth ₩1,100, children ₩1,000 (combined Busosanseong & Goransa; free for Buyeo residents and those 65+). Open daily, summer 09:00–18:00, winter 09:00–17:00. Intermediate point names follow general guides.
events: 72nd Baekje Cultural Festival (around Jeongnimsa Temple Site and Gwanbuk-ri Site, Buyeo) — ended

t047.name: Daejeon Gyejoksan Red Clay Trail
t047.sub: 14.5 km red clay path walked barefoot
t047.hours: 5–6 hours for the full trail (many shorter options)
t047.how: Daejeon city bus toward Jangdong (check routes); free parking at the forest area
t047.turn: Loop along a forest road — turn back where it suits your fitness, e.g. at the forest-road junction pavilion
t047.toiletNote: Not confirmed in official sources (foot-washing stations and rest areas are found along the way)
t047.notes: 14.5 km in total; the Jangdong → Gyejoksanseong → Seongjaesan → Sandi Village traverse is about 10 km / 4 hours, and there is also a 4.1 km course from Beopdong Residents' Rest Park (Telltrip). Inside Gyejoksanseong and some hiking paths are closed for works.
events: Sunyang Gyejoksan Barefoot Festival (resumed after 7 years) — ended
Weekend forest concerts every spring–autumn (check dates)

t048.name: Cheonan Independence Hall Maple Tree Forest Trail
t048.how: City bus to Independence Hall from Cheonan Station or Cheonan Bus Terminal
points: Around the Grand Hall of the Nation
Forest path behind the exhibition halls
t048.notes: Free admission, paid parking (small cars ₩2,000). Mar–Oct 09:30–18:00 (last entry 17:30), Nov–Feb until 17:00. Closed Mondays (open if a public holiday). Intermediate point names follow general guides.
events: Maple Tree Forest Trail night opening every autumn (check dates; in 2025, 10 Oct – 9 Nov, Fri–Sun 18:00–21:00)

t049.name: Byeonsan Masil-gil Trail Course 3: Jeokbyeokgang Sunset Trail
t049.how: From Buan Terminal, take a rural bus toward Gyeokpo and get off around Seongcheon (check timetable)
t049.turn: One-way — return by bus from Gyeokpo Port. Linking with Course 12 makes a loop around Gyeokpo
t049.notes: The draft's 'Gyeokpo Chaeseokgang–Jeokbyeokgang section' officially corresponds to Course 3 'Jeokbyeokgang Sunset Trail' (Seongcheon → Gyeokpo Port, 9.8 km). Always open, free. Check the tides (low tide) before viewing the coastal rock at Chaeseokgang and Jeokbyeokgang. Enquiries: Buan-gun 063-580-4545

t050.name: Naejangsan Autumn Foliage Trail
t050.sub: Uhwajeong Pavilion, maple tunnel, Naejangsa Temple
t050.how: Bus No. 171 from Jeongeup Station (about 45 min) or taxi (about 20 min). Vehicle access is difficult in the autumn peak season
t050.turn: Round trip — return the same way (maple tunnel) from Naejangsa, or use the cable car from Uhwajeong to the observatory
t050.toiletNote: Toilets listed as available in the Uhwajeong (Naejangsan) tourist information — check exact location on site
t050.notes: Corrected the draft order (ticket office → Naejangsa → Uhwajeong): the actual order is ticket office → Uhwajeong → maple tunnel → Iljumun → Naejangsa. Section distance not confirmed in official sources (estimated about 3 km). Paid parking (weekends, small/mid-size cars ₩5,000). Check national park notices for foliage-season traffic control and shuttles. Last entry to the mountain: Apr–Oct 16:00, Nov–Mar 15:00
events: 2026 Naejangsan Seoraebong section reservation system (Seorae Visitor Support Center – Seoraebong – Byeongnyeonam, 2.8 km, 520 people per day)
Naejangsan peak foliage and foliage festival every Oct–Nov (check dates)

t051.name: Suncheonman Wetland Reed Trail
t051.sub: Mujingyo Bridge, reed-bed boardwalk, Yongsan Observatory
t051.how: City bus to Suncheonman Wetland from Suncheon Station or terminal (check routes), or taxi
t051.turn: Round trip — return the same way from Yongsan Observatory to the ticket office
points: Boardwalk up to Yongsan Observatory (about 908 m)
t051.toiletNote: Toilets listed as available in Suncheonman Wetland tourist information — check exact location on site
t051.notes: Admission adults ₩10,000 (combined with the National Garden). Hours: Mar–Apr & Sep–Oct 08:00–18:00, May–Aug 08:00–19:00, Nov–Feb 08:00–17:00. Closed the last Monday of each month. The old observatory was rated grade D and demolished; the new Yongsan Observatory opened 2025-07-11. Round-trip distance is an estimate
events: Suncheonman reed-related events every autumn (check dates)

t052.name: Damyang Juknokwon – Gwanbangjerim – Metasequoia Road
t052.sub: Bamboo grove, embankment forest, tree-lined road
t052.how: From U-Square in Gwangju, take an intercity bus to Damyang or city bus No. 311, get off at Damyang-eup and walk
t052.turn: One-way — from the Metasequoia Road return by taxi (about ₩5,000 to Juknokwon) or walk about 40 min
t052.notes: Juknokwon adults ₩3,000 (Mar–Oct 09:00–19:00), Metasequoia Road adults ₩2,000, Gwanbangjerim free and always open. Total distance is an estimate summed from sections
events: Damyang Bamboo Festival every May (check dates)

t053.name: Gochang Seonunsa Temple → Dosoram Hermitage
t053.sub: Dosol Valley, Jangsasong Pine, rock-carved Buddha
t053.start: Seonunsan Provincial Park parking lot (Seonunsa entrance)
t053.how: County bus to Seonunsa from Gochang Public Bus Terminal. By car, Seonunsan IC on the Seohaean Expressway
t053.turn: Round trip — return the same way from Dosoram; if you have the energy, loop back via Nakjodae and Cheonmabong (parking – Cheonmabong about 4.7 km)
t053.toiletNote: Toilets listed as available in Seonunsa tourist information — check exact location on site
t053.notes: Official Seonunsa–Dosoram distance not confirmed (estimated about 3 km, almost flat). Parking free for 30 min, then ₩2,000. Enquiries: Seonunsan management office
events: Seonunsa red spider lily (kkotmureut) blooming season every September (check dates)

t054.name: Geumodo Bireong-gil Trail Course 1
t054.how: Ferry to Hamgumi (Sina Shipping) from Yeosu Ferry Terminal (Jungang-dong) or Baegyahang Port. Ferries from Singihang go to Yeocheonhang, so they don't connect directly with Course 1
t054.turn: One-way — continue on Course 2 from Dupo, or return to the dock by island bus/taxi
t054.toiletNote: Toilets at Hamgumi (public, leased at the dock), Dupo Beach and Dupo (480-4 Geumoseobu-ro) — per Yeosu-si Geumodo information
t054.notes: Difficulty: easy. Yeosu → Hamgumi adults ₩15,150 (50% discount listed for out-of-town tourists), Baegyahang → Hamgumi ₩7,500. Summer (1 Apr – 15 Oct) and winter timetables differ (from 16 Oct changes to 3 sailings). Check for weather cancellations

t055.name: Cheongsando Slow-gil Trail Course 1
t055.sub: Docheong Port → Seopyeonje filming site → Hwarangpo
t055.how: Ferry to Cheongsando from Wando Port Coastal Ferry Terminal, about 50 min (adults ₩8,700 one-way)
t055.turn: One-way — continue on Course 2, or return to Docheong Port by Slow City circular bus/taxi
points: Seopyeonje filming hill · red clay path
t055.notes: The Slow-gil has 11 courses totalling 42.195 km. Course 1 distance (5.7 km) not checked directly on the official page. Ferries are crowded in April during the canola and green barley peak. Reports of a 50% fare discount from 2026-04-01 (ends when funds run out)
events: 2026 Cheongsando Slow Walking Festival (ended)

t056.name: Haenam Dalmagodo Trail
t056.how: County bus to Mihwangsa from Haenam Bus Terminal (check timetable)
points: Junction with Ttangkkeut Millennium Forest Old Road (end of Course 3)
t056.notes: By course: Course 1 2.71 / Course 2 4.37 / Course 3 5.63 / Course 4 5.03 km. Free, always open. Scree sections — hiking boots recommended. Official walking time not confirmed. Enquiries: Haenam-gun Tourism Office 061-530-5159
events: 2026 Dalmagodo Healing Walk (ended)

t057.name: Mudeungsan Old Trail Section 2
t057.how: City bus to Wonhyosa from central Gwangju (e.g. No. 1187; check routes), get off at the terminus
t057.turn: Descend from Seoseokdae via Jangbuljae (loop back to Wonhyo station about 10.9 km / 4.5 hours) or return the same way
t057.notes: Draft 4.12 km → 4.2 km per tourist information. Stony path to about halfway, then dirt path. Large elevation gain, rated 'difficult'. Always open. Enquiries: Mudeungsan National Park 062-227-1187

t058.name: Mokpo Yudalsan Dulle-gil Trail
t058.sub: Dalseongsa Temple, Sculpture Park, sunset viewpoint
t058.start: Yudalsan parking lot (in front of Nojeokbong)
t058.how: About 15–20 min walk from Mokpo Station, or city bus (check routes)
t058.turn: Loop (back near the start between parking lot and rest area)
t058.notes: The route via the summit (Ildeungbawi) is separate (Eomin Hill – Ildeungbawi – Gwanungak – Dalseongsa). The Dulle-gil is mostly gentle

t059.name: Jangseong Chungnyeongsan Cypress Forest Trail Section 1
t059.how: County bus toward Seosam-myeon or taxi from Jangseong Station or Jangseong Terminal (check timetable)
t059.turn: One-way — return by taxi from Geumgok, or continue on Sections 2–4 to make a loop (about 23.6 km in total)
points: Haneulsup-gil (Chuam-ri, 860 m barrier-free boardwalk) — optional detour
t059.notes: Four Dulle-gil sections: Section 1 Moam – Geumgok 9 km, Section 2 Geumgok – Goejeong 6.3 km, Section 3 Goejeong – Daedeok junction 4.5 km, Section 4 Daedeok – Moam 3.8 km (easiest). Organised by official sections instead of the draft's single 'Healing Forest' starting point

t060.name: Busan Igidae Coastal Walk
t060.sub: Oryukdo → Dongsaengmal, part of Haeparang-gil Trail Course 1
t060.how: City bus toward Oryukdo from Kyungsung Univ.·Pukyong Nat'l Univ. Station (check routes). In the reverse direction, buses 20, 22, 24, 27, 39, 131 to 'Igidae Entrance'
t060.turn: One-way — from Dongsaengmal / Igidae Entrance return by bus (20, 22, 24, 27, 39, 131) to Kyungsung Univ.·Pukyong Nat'l Univ. Station
t060.toiletNote: Toilets at Oryukdo Sunrise Park (tourist information). Toilets along the walk not confirmed in official sources
t060.notes: Free, always open. Night lighting on Dongsaengmal – Eoulmadang 1.26 km (sunset–22:00). Some steep and windy sections — trekking shoes recommended. The first part of Haeparang-gil Course 1 (Oryukdo – Mipo). Order of intermediate points partly estimated
events: 2026 Korea Dulle-gil × East-West Trail Walking Travel Week, Nam-gu Busan 'Oryukdo Safe Walking Road' (ended)
Durunubi Haeparang-gil QR stamps and completion certification run year-round (check)

t061.name: Haeundae Blueline Park Coastal Walk
t061.sub: Mipo → Cheongsapo → Songjeong along the old Donghae Nambu Line
t061.how: About 15 min walk from Haeundae Station (Busan Line 2)
t061.turn: One-way — return from Songjeong by Beach Train (paid) or bus
t061.notes: 4.8 km stretch of the old Donghae Nambu Line. The Beach Train and Sky Capsule (Mipo – Cheongsapo about 2 km) are paid; from 2026-05-01 the first Beach Train runs at 09:00. The walkway is free
events: Durunubi Haeparang-gil QR stamps (Mipo, end of Course 1 · Course 2) run year-round (check)

t062.name: Yeongdo Taejongdae Loop Road
t062.how: Bus 8, 30, 88 or 186 from Nampo-dong, or 88 or 101 from Busan Station, to Taejongdae
t062.notes: The Danubi train is suspended for safety inspection (resumption undecided). Free replacement loop bus Wed–Sun 09:30–17:30 (no service Mon–Tue). Loop length listed variously as 3.8 km / 4.3 km. Sinseon Rock closed due to rockfall. Yeongdo Lighthouse marine culture space 10:00–17:00, closed Mondays. Coastal pebble beach closed from about 20:00

t063.name: Yeongdo Huinnyeoul Culture Village & Jeoryeong Coastal Walk
t063.how: Bus 6, 7, 9, 71, 82, 85 or 508 from Yeongdodaegyo Bridge, or 82, 85 or 508 from Busan Station
t063.end: Southern end of Jeoryeong Coastal Walk
t063.turn: Round trip, or one-way and return by bus
t063.notes: Residential area — mind noise and photo etiquette. Jeoryeong Coastal Walk public parking about 100 spaces (₩200 per 10 min). Sinseon 3-dong public parking under a 5-day rotation system from Apr 2026. Distance about 3 km (per news articles)

t064.name: Geumjeongsanseong East Gate → North Gate → Beomeosa Temple
t064.how: Bus 203 toward Sanseong Village from around Oncheonjang Station, get off at the East Gate (check routes)
t064.turn: One-way — from the Beomeosa ticket office bus stop, take bus 90 back to Beomeosa Station (Line 1)
t064.notes: Geumjeongsan was designated Korea's 24th national park (urban type) on 2025-10-31. Section distances not confirmed in official sources (estimated). A round trip from the North Gate to Godangbong (801.5 m) can be added, but it has rocky and steel-stair sections. Makgeolli in Sanseong Village after the descent

t065.name: Ulsan Daewangam Park Coastal Walk
t065.sub: Suspension bridge, Daewangam rocks, pine grove
t065.how: City bus to Daewangam Park from central Ulsan (check routes)
points: Black pine grove path (entrance – Daewangam about 600 m)
t065.notes: Suspension bridge free, 09:00–18:00 (no access at night). Closing days need official confirmation. Loop distance is an estimate
events: 2026 Korea Dulle-gil Walking Travel Week, Dong-gu Ulsan 'Haeparang Shelter experience' (ended)

t066.name: Ulsan Taehwagang Simni Bamboo Forest
t066.sub: Taehwagang National Garden, Eunhasu-gil (Milky Way Path)
t066.how: City bus via Taehwagang National Garden from Ulsan Station (KTX), Taehwagang Station or the bus terminal
t066.end: End of Simni Bamboo Forest (toward Taehwaru Pavilion)
t066.turn: Round trip, or loop back along the opposite riverbank
points: Toilets and rest facilities in the garden
t066.toiletNote: Toilets and rest facilities throughout the garden (per news articles) — check locations on site
t066.notes: Eunhasu-gil lit from sunset to 23:00. Free. Garden opening hours need official confirmation

t067.name: Yeongnam Alps Ganwoljae Silver Grass Trail
t067.sub: Deer farm forest road → Ganwoljae Pass
t067.hours: About 2 hours one-way (about 4 hours round trip)
t067.start: Baenaegol Deer Farm (Baenae 2 Public Parking Lot)
t067.how: Driving recommended (navigation: 'Baenae 2 Public Parking Lot'). Check public transport routes
t067.turn: Round trip — return the same forest road from Ganwoljae (about 6 km)
t067.notes: Starting from Deungeok Hot Spring complex means a steep mountain path. Ganwoljae rest area sells cup noodles and drinks. Weekend parking is crowded in silver grass season
events: Ganwoljae silver grass peak and Ulju Mountain Film Festival etc. every autumn (Sep–Oct) (check dates)

t068.name: Gyeongju Namsan Samneung → Geumobong → Yongjang
t068.sub: Samneung Valley rock-carved Buddhas, Yongjangsa Temple Site
t068.how: City bus in the 500s (500, 505, 506, 507, 508) from central Gyeongju to Samneung (check routes)
t068.turn: One-way — return by city bus from Yongjang Village
points: Stone Seated Buddha in Samneung Valley
t068.notes: Namsan District of Gyeongju National Park. Rocky climb from Sangseonam to Geumobong. Total distance not confirmed in official sources (estimated). Yongjanggol valley path about 3 km

t069.name: Gyeongju Daereungwon – Cheomseongdae – Donggung Palace & Wolji Pond
t069.how: About 15–20 min walk or city bus from Gyeongju Station (not Singyeongju Station) or the intercity bus terminal
t069.turn: One-way — return to the city centre by bus or on foot from Donggung & Wolji
t069.notes: Donggung & Wolji charges admission (check fee on site); famous night view. Seasonal flower fields around Cheomseongdae
events: 2026 Gyeongju Daereungwon Stone Wall Road Festival (ended)

t070.name: Gyeongju Bomun Lake Dulle-gil Trail
t070.how: City bus to Bomun Complex from Gyeongju Station or terminal (e.g. 10, 18, 100, 150; check)
t070.notes: Bomun Lake circumference about 8 km; recommended loop 7 km / 2 hours. About 1 hour by bicycle
events: Gyeongju cherry blossoms (around Bomun Lake) peak in early April every year (check dates)

t071.name: Pohang Homi Peninsula Coastal Dulle-gil Trail
t071.how: City bus toward Donghae-myeon / Homigot from central Pohang (check routes)
t071.turn: One-way — return by city bus from Homigot. Walking it in separate courses is recommended
t071.notes: Courses 1–4 total about 25 km (24.7); linked with the Haeparang-gil it runs 58 km to Janggi-myeon. Free, always open; no entry during weather warnings. The start coordinates are the tourist information's representative point (Donghae-myeon) and may differ from the actual Course 1 start. Enquiries: Pohang-si 054-270-3203

t072.name: Yeongdeok Blue Road Course B: Blue Snow Crab Trail
t072.how: From Yeongdeok Terminal, take a rural bus toward Ganggu / Chuksan and get off at Haemaji Park (check timetable)
t072.turn: One-way — return to Yeongdeok-eup by bus from Chuksan Port
t072.notes: The 'highlight' of the Blue Road's four courses (64.6 km). Watch for slippery coastal rock sections. Order of villages passed is estimated from place names
events: 29th Yeongdeok Snow Crab Festival (Ganggu Haeparang Park, ended)

t073.name: Uljin Geumgang Pine Forest Trail Section 1
t073.how: Use the meeting point given when you book. Public transport is inconvenient — car or taxi
t073.turn: One-way — return to the start by operator vehicle/taxi from the end point (confirm when booking)
t073.notes: Advance reservation and a guide are required; one section at a time only. Check group size, fees and booking via Uljin-gun / Korea Forest Service official guidance. Section 1 is part of the peddlers' route from Uljin Heungbu Market to Bonghwa Chunyang Market
events: 2026 Geumgang Pine Forest Trail operating period (reservation, guided)

t074.name: Cheongsong Juwangsan Daejeonsa Temple → Yongchu Falls
t074.how: Rural bus to Juwangsan from Cheongsong Terminal, get off at the terminus and walk
t074.turn: Round trip — return the same way from Yongchu Falls. Can be extended to Jeolgu Falls and Yongyeon Falls
t074.notes: Mountain entry hours: summer (Apr–Oct) 04:00–15:00, winter (Nov–Mar) 05:00–14:00. Reservation system for Jeolgol – Gamebong (5.7 km) in Oct–Nov (by 17:00 the day before). Official Daejeonsa – Yongchu distance not confirmed (estimated about 2 km)
events: Juwangsan autumn foliage peak season every Oct–Nov (check dates)

t075.name: Andong Hahoe Village & Buyongdae Cliff
t075.sub: Village stone-wall lanes, ferry boat, Buyongdae view
t075.how: Bus 210 or Express 2 from Andong Station or terminal to Hahoe Village (Market), then free shuttle about 10 min
t075.turn: From Buyongdae cross back to the village by ferry boat, then shuttle to the ticket office
t075.notes: Admission adults ₩5,000; last entry Apr–Sep 17:30, Oct–Mar 16:30; free parking. Ferry suspended depending on weather and water level. Distance estimated
events: Andong International Mask Dance Festival every late Sep – early Oct (check 2026 dates)

t076.name: Mungyeong Saejae Gwageo-gil (Scholars' Road)
t076.start: Mungyeong Saejae Provincial Park parking lot · 1st Gate
t076.how: Bus to Mungyeong Saejae or taxi from Mungyeong Bus Terminal (Mungyeong-eup)
t076.turn: Round trip — return the same dirt road from Joryeonggwan (or turn back at the 2nd Gate depending on fitness: about 7 km round trip from the parking lot)
t076.notes: Park and parking free (parking lot 08:30–17:30), trail always open. Open film set adults ₩2,000, park electric tram adults ₩2,000. Red clay path suitable for barefoot walking
events: 2026 Mungyeong Traditional Chasabal (Tea Bowl) Festival (ended)
Mungyeong Saejae Barefoot Festival every year (check dates)

t077.name: Yeongju Sobaeksan Jarak-gil Trail Section 1
t077.sub: Sosu Seowon → Jukgye Gugok → Choamsa → Dalbatgol
t077.how: Bus 27 from Yeongju or Punggi to Seonbi Village (Sosu Seowon) (check timetable)
t077.turn: One-way — from Samga-ri bus stop, bus 26 to Punggi, bus 27 back to Seonbi Village
t077.notes: The draft's 'Sosu Seowon → Choamsa' is only part of Section 1. The official Section 1 is 12.6 km to Samga parking lot. Bus information is from a 2011 article, so check the latest timetable

t078.name: Tongyeong Somaemuldo Lighthouse Trail
t078.how: Ferry from Geoje Jeogu Port (Maemuldo Ferry Terminal, free parking) or Tongyeong Port. Bring ID
t078.turn: Loop (back to start) — if the Yeolmokgae tide doesn't suit, turn back at the Lighthouse Island observatory
t078.toiletNote: A toilet is mentioned via the 'crossroads junction above the toilet' above the dock (Kookje Shinmun hiking article) — otherwise not confirmed in official sources
t078.notes: Yeolmokgae can be crossed only at low tide, twice a day — check the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency tide table, then book your return ferry. Summer: departs Jeogu Port 08:30 & 11:00, departs Somaemuldo 14:30 & 16:15 (per a 2022 article; check the latest)

t079.name: Geoje Windy Hill & Sinseondae
t079.how: Bus toward Haegeumgang from Gohyeon Terminal (check routes), get off at Dojangpo, or drive
t079.turn: Round trip — return from Sinseondae to Dojangpo
t079.toiletNote: Toilets provided at Windy Hill (per news articles)
t079.notes: Dojangpo free parking is often full at weekends; paid parking in front of Windy Hill (₩3,000 per day). Haegeumgang cruise boats leave from Dojangpo dock. Total distance estimated

t080.name: Namhae Baraegil Trail Course 11: Darangi Jiget-gil
t080.how: County bus to Gacheon from Namhae Public Bus Terminal (check timetable)
t080.turn: One-way — return by county bus from Pyeongsan Port
t080.notes: Renumbered from old Baraegil Course 1 to current main-line Course 11. Tourist information describes it in the Gacheon → Pyeongsan direction (the draft's Pyeongsan Port → Gacheon is the reverse; either works). Enquiries: Namhae Baraegil Visitor Center 055-863-8778

t081.name: Hadong Simni Cherry Blossom Road
t081.how: County bus to Hwagae from Hadong Terminal, or a bus via Gurye / Hwagae
t081.turn: One-way — return to Hwagae Market by county bus from the Ssanggyesa entrance
t081.notes: Heavy traffic in cherry blossom season — public transport and walking recommended
events: 28th Hadong Hwagae Market Cherry Blossom Festival (ended)

t082.name: Jinjuseong Fortress Wall Trail
t082.how: About 10 min walk from Jinju Intercity Bus Terminal
t082.notes: Wall circumference 1,760 m. Admission adults ₩2,000 (free for Jinju residents). Summer (Mar–Oct) 05:00–23:00, winter 05:00–22:00
events: 2026 Jinju Namgang Yudeung (Lantern) Festival (ended)
75th Gaecheon Art Festival (ended)

t083.name: Jinhae Dream Road: Cheonjabong Haeoreum-gil
t083.how: Bus via Anmin Pass or taxi from central Changwon / Jinhae (check routes)
t083.turn: One-way — descend from below Cheonjabong to central Jinhae, then bus
points: Junction with Section 3 Baegil Achimgoyo Sangil
t083.notes: Dream Road has 4 sections, 26.4 km in total (Jangboksan Sculpture Park – Anmin Pass – Cheonjabong – Baegil – Sosa). 6–8 m wide forest road, so gentle. Information is from a 2015 article — check current section names and distances with Changwon-si
events: 64th Jinhae Gunhangje Festival (ended)

t084.name: Hapcheon Haeinsa Sori-gil Trail
t084.how: Bus to Haeinsa from Hapcheon or Daegu Seobu Bus Stop, get off near Daejanggyeong Theme Park (check)
t084.turn: One-way — return by bus from the Haeinsa parking lot / terminal
t084.notes: Distance listed variously (6.3 km in a 2013 article, about 7.3 km in a 2026 article) — the latest 7.3 km is used. Check Haeinsa admission on site

t085.name: Goseong Sangjogam Dinosaur Footprint Coastal Trail
t085.sub: Dinosaur Museum, Sangjogam Rock, Byeongpung Rock
t085.start: Sangjogam County Park parking lot (Sangjogam cruise parking lot)
t085.how: County bus to Sangjogam from Goseong Terminal (check timetable) or drive
t085.turn: One-way — county bus/taxi from Maekjeonpo Port, or turn back at Byeongpung Rock Observatory
points: Dinosaur and bird footprint fossil site (Natural Monument No. 411)
t085.notes: Dinosaur footprints are exposed at low tide — check the tides. Coastal access closed at high tide. Distance not confirmed in official sources (estimated)
events: 2026 Korea Dulle-gil Walking Travel Week, Goseong (Gyeongnam) 'Natural Man Road' (ended)

t086.name: Saryeoni Forest Trail

yt01.name: Incheon Dulle-gil Trail Course 1 (Gyeyangsan)
yt01.sub: Forest loop 5 min from the subway
yt01.start: Near Gyeyang Mountain Fortress Museum (5 min walk from Gyesan Station Exits 5 & 6)
yt01.how: About 5 min walk from Gyesan Station Exits 5 & 6 (Incheon Line 1); also accessible from Imhak Station
yt01.notes: Distance varies between sources from 6.3 to 7.4 km. The Incheon city official page describes it as a loop starting at Yeonmujeong; for the stamp book and completion certification, contact Incheon city (032-710-2132). Free admission.

yt02.name: Dutasan Betlebawi Sanseong-gil Trail
yt02.how: Use Mureung Valley parking lot (about 600 spaces, cars ₩2,000)
yt02.end: Back to Mureung Valley ticket office
yt02.turn: Loop — Betlebawi → Sanseong 12 Falls → Macheonnu → Yongchu Falls → descend to Mureung Valley
yt02.notes: Mureung Valley admission adults ₩4,000 (some sources say ₩2,000 — check on site). Ticket office 09:00–20:00 (summer) / until 18:00 (winter). Trails may be closed during the wildfire-prevention period (033-539-3700). About 60 min to Betlebawi Observatory, then steep slopes and rocky ridges. The 11 km / 5–6 hours is from the video description; Korea Tourism Organization lists 14.9 km / 4 h 20 min via Dutasanseong.

yt03.name: Goesan Sanmagi Old Road
yt03.sub: Old lakeside road along Goesan Lake + Lake Trail
yt03.start: Noru Spring (start of Course 1) · Sanmagi Old Road parking lot
yt03.how: About 25 min from Goesan IC or Yeonpung IC; parking small/mid-size cars ₩3,000
yt03.turn: One-way — from Sanmagi Village return by cruise boat (Chadol Rock, Sanmagi Village, Yeonhahyeop Suspension Bridge piers) or the same way
yt03.notes: Open 09:00–17:00 (Sanmagi Lake Trail until 18:00). Connects with the Sanmagi Lake Trail opened in 2025 (about 10 km loop); the Gongdogyo Bridge section is open only on weekends and public holidays. Cruise boats stop in winter and resume in mid-March (043-832-3527). Walking time not confirmed in official sources.

yt04.name: Inje Gombaeryeong
yt04.start: Jeombongsan Forest Ecology Management Center (Gangseon Village trailhead)
yt04.how: Driving recommended; arrive in time for your reserved entry time
yt04.turn: Turn back at the summit (Gombaeryeong) — Course 1 ascent 5.1 km, Course 2 descent 5.4 km
yt04.notes: Advance reservation required on Supnadeuri-e (foresttrip.go.kr), free, once a month per person, up to 4 people. Closed Mon–Tue. Summer (21 Apr – 31 Oct) entry at 09:00, 10:00, 11:00; winter (16 Dec – 28 Feb) at 10:00, 11:00. Descend by 14:00 (Course 1) / 13:30 (Course 2). Closed during wildfire-prevention periods (1 Feb – 15 May, 1 Nov – 15 Dec) — may be closed from 2026-11-01.

yt05.name: Jeongseon Mindungsan Silver Grass Trail
yt05.sub: Jeungsan Elementary course, silvery silver grass
yt05.how: Near Mindungsan Station. During the festival, vehicles are fully banned from Balgudeok — use Mindungsan Sports Ground or Neungjeon (No. 2) parking lot; no station shuttle (discontinued from 2026-08-01)
yt05.end: Back to Jeungsan Elementary (same way down)
yt05.turn: Turn back at Mindungsan summit (1,118.8 m)
points: Silver grass field at Mindungsan summit (1,118.8 m)
yt05.notes: Distance differs between sources: Jeungsan Elementary → summit about 3.2 km (1 h 30 min – 2 hours one-way); Korea Tourism Organization lists about 9 km / 4 hours round trip via Balgudeok; a Korail package lists 4 km / 3–3.5 hours round trip. Silver grass peaks mid-October – early November. Jeongseon tourist information 1544-9053.
events: 2026 Mindungsan Silver Grass Festival (ongoing)

yt06.name: Pocheon Myeongseongsan Silver Grass Trail
yt06.hours: About 4 hours (about 2 h 30 min if turning back at the pavilion)
yt06.how: Start from Sanjeong Lake Sangdong parking lot
yt06.turn: Turn back at the octagonal pavilion where the silver grass begins, or at the summit area
yt06.notes: Course 1 (Deungnyong Falls) suits beginners. Course 2 along the Chaekbawi ridge (5.2 km / 3 h 30 min) has rocky ridges and steel stairs. Course 3 (toward Jainsa) is closed due to damage. The summit silver grass field covers about 198,000 m².
events: 29th Pocheon Sanjeong Lake Myeongseongsan Silver Grass Festival (ended)

yt09.name: Ongjin Guleopdo Gaemeori Hill
yt09.hours: Overnight (2 days) recommended (trekking on the island)
yt09.how: Incheon Port Coastal Ferry Terminal or Daebudo Bangameori → Deokjeokdo (fast ferry about 1 h 10 min) → transfer to the Narae ferry (odd-numbered days about 1 hour, even-numbered days 2+ hours)
yt09.end: Gaemeori Hill (western tip of the island)
yt09.turn: Return the same way from Gaemeori Hill to Keunmal
yt09.toiletNote: Public toilet near Keunmal beach (Wikitree article, Apr 2026). Not confirmed elsewhere on the island, including Gaemeori Hill
yt09.notes: Frequent weather cancellations — check sailings before departure. Wild deer roam; keep your distance in breeding season. Tokkiseom is reachable only at low tide. Check camping rules with Ongjin-gun. Trekking distance not confirmed in official sources (km left blank).

yt10.name: Tongyeong Saryangdo Jirisan (Jirimangsan) Ridge Traverse
yt10.sub: No. 1 island hike, twin suspension bridges
yt10.start: Donji Village (trail to the left of Donji branch school)
yt10.how: Ferry Gaochi Port → Geumpyeong Port about 40 min, village bus between Geumpyeong and Donji / Goseong Yongampo → Naeji Port about 20 min
yt10.turn: One-way — return by ferry from Jinchon / Geumpyeong Port
points: Twin suspension bridges between Hyangbong and Yeonjibong (39 m · 22 m)
yt10.notes: Dalbawi – Oknyeobong has dangerous steep slopes and rocky ridges; beginners should use the bypass. Ferries from Gaochi Port every 2 hours on weekdays, hourly on weekends / in summer (Mar–Nov). Distance and time are from a 2009 Seoul Shinmun article and may differ now.

yt11.name: Ulleungdo Haengnam Coastal Walk
yt11.start: Breakwater behind Dodong Port Ferry Terminal
yt11.how: Straight after getting off the ferry at Dodong Port; cars use the public parking near Dodong Port
yt11.turn: One-way — return from Chotdae Rock by bus (about hourly) or taxi, or loop back via Dodong Old Road
yt11.notes: Haean Nuri-gil Course 34. History of partial and full closures of the Haengnam Lighthouse section due to rockfall risk (full closure reported April 2026) — be sure to check with Ulleung-gun Office 054-791-2191 / tourist information 054-790-6454 before visiting.

yt12.name: Deogyusan Hyangjeokbong (Gondola Course)
yt12.hours: About 40 min (Seolcheonbong ↔ Hyangjeokbong round trip, gondola extra)

yt12.turn: Turn back at Hyangjeokbong → gondola down from Seolcheonbong (can extend to Jungbong)
yt12.notes: Seolcheonbong → Hyangjeokbong about 600 m / 20 min, gentle slope. Gondola adults ₩22,000 round trip / ₩17,000 one-way (call ahead to check operation and reservations). Famous for winter snow flowers. Deogyusan National Park Office 063-322-3174.

points: Suspension bridge (about 52 m, 510 m above sea level)
yt16.notes: km is for the suspension bridge round trip (about 900 m one-way); Cheonhwangbong section distance not confirmed in official sources. Steep stone steps. Mountain entry Apr–Oct 05:00–15:00, Nov–Mar 06:00–14:00. Closed during weather warnings (061-473-5210).

yt17.name: Sobaeksan Eouigok – Birobong
yt17.hours: About 4 h 20 min (round trip, 2 h 10 min one-way)
yt17.end: Back to Eouigok Visitor Support Center
yt17.turn: Turn back at Birobong (1,439 m) — or descend to Cheondong Visitor Support Center (Cheondong–Eouigok 11.6 km / 4 h 40 min)
yt17.notes: Per Korea Tourism Organization, Eouigok → Birobong is 5.1 km / 2 h 10 min (one-way). Famous for biting winter winds and rime frost; royal azaleas in May–June. Check closures during the wildfire-prevention period.

yt18.name: Changnyeong Hwawangsan Silver Grass Fortress Trail
yt18.sub: Vast silver grass field, Hwawangsanseong Fortress
yt18.how: Okcheon parking lot 550 spaces; parking and admission free
yt18.turn: One-way traverse — descend to Jahagok parking lot (378 spaces). A round trip from Jahagok is the shortest (straight to the silver grass plateau and South Gate)
points: Hwawangsanseong East Gate · silver grass field
yt18.notes: Distance and time are estimates from a 2015 Kyongbuk Maeil hiking article (Gwallyongsa – Jahagok). Silver grass field about 56,000 pyeong. Watch for steep slopes and scree on the Jahagok descent. The video follows the Jahagok round trip (Trails 1 & 3).
events: Hwawangsan silver grass season every autumn (check festival/event dates)

yt19.name: Yeongwol Donggang Jatbong & Eoarayeon
yt19.sub: Donggang's finest scenery, national scenic site
yt19.start: In front of Geoun branch school (Jatbong / Eoarayeon fork)
yt19.toiletNote: Toilets available (Korea Tourism Organization information; exact location not confirmed)
yt19.notes: Check in advance whether it is closed during the spring/autumn wildfire-prevention periods (033-370-2426). Beware of the Donggang River rising quickly after the rainy season. Free admission and parking.

yt20.name: Daejeon Jangtaesan Natural Recreation Forest
yt20.start: Jangtaesan Natural Recreation Forest parking lot
points: Skyway · Sky Tower (temporarily closed for safety inspection)
yt20.notes: Free admission and parking, open every day. Suspension bridge hours: Mar–Jun & Sep–Oct 09:00–18:00, Jul–Aug until 19:00, Nov–Feb until 17:00. Skyway (196 m) and Sky Tower temporarily closed for safety inspection (per an Aug 2026 article). Walking distance not confirmed in official sources (km left blank).

yt21.name: Geochang Udusan Y-shaped Suspension Bridge
yt21.sub: Korea's first Y-shaped towerless suspension bridge
yt21.turn: Loop — can be combined with a hike to Uisangbong / Udusan summit
yt21.toiletNote: Toilets available (Korea Tourism Organization information; exact location not confirmed)
yt21.notes: Closed every Tuesday. Admission ₩3,000 (ages 7 to under 65). Suspension bridge Mar–Oct 09:00–17:50, Nov–Feb until 16:50. Course distance not confirmed in official sources (km left blank).

yt22.name: Gunsan Gogunsan Seom-it-gil (Island-Linking Trail)
yt22.how: Jangjado public parking lot → boat to Bangchukdo / Myeongdo from Jangjado pier (often sold out even on weekdays; booking via app recommended). There is also a route from Gunsan Coastal Ferry Terminal
yt22.turn: One-way — return from Maldo by boat to Jangjado; you can turn back midway at Myeongdo Port
points: Bangchukdo Dongnimmun Rock · suspension bridge (83 m)
Traveller rest area at Maldo pier
yt22.notes: Total length differs between sources (Segye Ilbo 8.64 km / 7.3 km in reports / 7.7 km and 3 h 6 min measured in the video). Four sea footbridges (308, 410, 555, 83 m). Temporarily opened 2026-08-08 (iNews24) — check official opening, fees and hours with Gunsan-si. Little shade, so avoid long walks at midday (12:00–16:00). Steep slopes and rockfall risk on Gwangdaedo.
events: Gogunsan Seom-it-gil temporary opening (from 2026-08-08, end date undecided)

yt23.name: Yeongdeok Blue Road Course A (Road of Light and Wind)
yt23.sub: Coastal and mountain paths from Ganggu Port to Haemaji Park
yt23.how: Start from Ganggu Terminal or Ganggu Snow Crab Street; free parking
yt23.turn: One-way — return to Ganggu by bus or taxi from Haemaji Park
yt23.notes: Overlaps with the Yeongdeok section of the Haeparang-gil. Official Blue Road site blueroad.yd.go.kr; Yeongdeok-gun Culture & Tourism Division 054-730-6349. The video was uploaded in 2019; no recent video found.

yt24.name: Yangpyeong Mulsori-gil Trail Course 1
yt24.sub: Country roads from station to station
yt24.how: Start right after getting off at Yangsu Station (Gyeongui–Jungang Line)
yt24.turn: One-way — return by train from Sinwon Station
yt24.notes: The current Course 1 (Yangsu Station – Sinwon Station, 10.5 km / 3–4 hours) is per the Santa TV video description; not confirmed in official sources. When it opened in 2013, Course 1 was Yangsu Station – Guksu Station 13.8 km (Aju Business Daily); courses have since been reorganised. Course map and certification booklet ₩2,000 (unmanned vending machines at Yangsu, Sinwon stations etc.); check stamp locations for each course with the Mulsori-gil Center.
events: 2026 Mulsori-gil Walk Together (Course 5, ended)
Mulsori-gil Walk Together on the last Sunday of each month (8 times a year, except in extreme heat/cold — check dates)

yt25.name: Hongcheon Sutasa Sanso-gil Trail
yt25.turn: Loop (along the valley via Gwingso and back)
yt25.notes: Free admission and parking, open year-round. Watch for slippery valley rocks. Loop route based on videos and reviews (articles don't mention a loop).

yt26.name: Gapyeong Jathyanggi Pureunsup (Pine Nut Forest)

yt26.notes: Admission ₩1,000 (general). Closed every Monday. Apr–Oct 09:00–18:00, Nov–Mar 09:00–17:00. Total trail distance not confirmed in official sources (video title says 10 km), so km left blank.
